name: apply_patch
description: Apply a unified diff. Prefer `edit` for exact string replacements. `path` is required for a single-file patch without `+++` headers; omit it (or pass `.`) for a multi-file `diff --git` / `+++ b/…` patch. Native — no `patch(1)`.

patch_content.description: Unified diff (---/+++ headers optional for a single file; @@ hunks required)

path.description: File to patch when the diff has no +++ headers. Optional for multi-file diffs (use `.` or omit).

name: bash
description: Run a shell command. Long notes: `read agent://tools/bash`.

background.description: If true, start the command in the background and return a job id immediately

description.description: Short description of why this command is run (optional)

timeout.description: Timeout in seconds (default: 120; ignored when background=true)

guide:
Execute a shell command in the project environment.

Default: wait for stdout/stderr (timeout 120s).
`background=true` returns a job id immediately; use `bg` to list/read/kill.
Long-running non-catastrophic commands auto-detach after 20s unless
`[tools.bash] auto_background = false`. Catastrophic commands (rm -rf /,
git clean of home, …) stay in the foreground and still hit the permission gate.
Child processes do not inherit provider API keys. Detached output lives under
`.whycodes/scratch`, not the OS temp dir.

name: bg
description: Manage background shell jobs started with bash `background: true` or `schedule`. Actions: list (default), read (needs id), kill (needs id).

max_chars.description: Max characters of output for read (default 8000)

name: browser
description: Control a local Chromium/Chrome window (CDP). Actions: status, open, snapshot, click, type, wait, screenshot, close. Not in the core tool profile — use tool_search. The OS sandbox does not apply; domain allowlists do not apply inside the browser. Permission defaults to ask.

name: checkpoint
description: Mark the current conversation so a later `rewind` can collapse exploratory context into a short report. Use before a speculative investigation. Does not snapshot files.

goal.description: What you are about to investigate

name: code_mode
description: Transform or refactor code files

instruction.description: Natural language description of the transformation to apply

path.description: Path to the code file to transform

name: edit
description: Make targeted edits to a file. Prefer `from`/`to`/`insert_after` content tags from `read`/`grep` (`N tag|text`). `old_string` is the fallback: exact match, then unique whitespace-tolerant match (indent / extra spaces only — not typos). Curly quotes, dashes and CRLF line endings match their plain forms.

from.description: Content tag of the first line to replace (inclusive)

insert_after.description: Content tag after which to insert new_string (no deletion)

old_string.description: Exact text to find. Required unless from/to/insert_after is set.

path.description: Path to the file to edit

replace_all.description: Replace all occurrences of old_string (default: false)

to.description: Content tag of the last line to replace (inclusive). Omit for a single line.

guide:
Make targeted edits. Prefer `from`/`to`/`insert_after` tags from `read`/`grep`.
`old_string` is the fallback: exact match, then unique whitespace-tolerant match.
A `.ipynb` is edited as `read` shows it. A changed code cell loses its outputs;
a `# %% [code] cell:new` marker adds a cell, removing a block deletes one.

name: external_directory
description: Access files outside the project directory (requires permission)

action.description: Action to perform: 'read' to read a file, 'list' to list a directory

path.description: Path to the external file or directory

name: git_blame
description: Show what revision and author last modified each line of a file. Runs 'git blame' in the working directory.

file.description: Path to the file to blame (required)

line_end.description: End line number (1-based) to limit blame range

line_start.description: Start line number (1-based) to limit blame range

name: git_commit
description: Stage and commit changes to git. If files are provided, runs 'git add <files>' then 'git commit -m <message>'. If no files, runs 'git commit -a -m <message>'. Optionally push with 'git push'.

files.description: Optional list of files to stage and commit. If empty or omitted, commits all modified tracked files (git commit -a).

push.description: If true, push after committing with 'git push'

name: git_diff
description: Show changes between commits, commit and working tree, etc. Runs 'git diff' in the working directory.

path.description: Limit diff to a specific file or directory

name: git_log
description: Show commit logs. Runs 'git log --oneline' in the working directory.

author.description: Filter by author name or email

path.description: Limit to commits touching a specific file or directory

since.description: Show commits more recent than a date (e.g. '2024-01-01', '1 week ago')

name: git_status
description: Show the working tree status. Runs 'git status --short' in the working directory.

path.description: Limit status to a specific path

name: github_issue
description: Manage GitHub issues: create, list, view, close, reopen, or comment on issues.

action.description: Action to perform on GitHub issues

issue_number.description: Issue number (required for view, close, reopen, comment)

per_page.description: Results per page (for 'list' action, default: 30, max: 100)

state.description: Filter by state (for 'list' action, default: open)

token.description: GitHub token (optional). Falls back to GITHUB_TOKEN / GH_TOKEN, `gh auth login`, gh hosts.yml, or git credentials.

name: github_pr
description: Create, list, view, or merge GitHub Pull Requests via the REST API. Token: tool arg, GITHUB_TOKEN / GH_TOKEN, `gh auth login`, or stored git credentials.

action.description: Action to perform on pull requests

token.description: GitHub token (optional). Falls back to GITHUB_TOKEN / GH_TOKEN, `gh auth login`, gh hosts.yml, or git credentials.

name: glob
description: Find files by glob pattern under the project (e.g. `**/*.rs`, `crates/**/mod.rs`). Respects .gitignore; skips heavy dirs (target, node_modules, .git, …). Served from the live file index when warm. Prefer over shell find.

path.description: Root directory for the search (default: project root)

guide:
Find files by glob pattern under the project (e.g. `**/*.rs`).
Respects .gitignore; skips heavy dirs.

name: grep
description: Search file contents with regex (ripgrep engine, in-process — no `rg` binary). Respects .gitignore; skips binaries and heavy dirs (target, node_modules, .git, …). Literal queries prune files via the workspace content index before scanning. Prefer over shell grep for project code search. Hits are `path:line tag:text` so `edit` can name the line by tag.

context.description: Lines of context before/after each match (default: 0, max: 5)

path.description: Directory or file to search in (default: project root)

guide:
Search file contents with regex (in-process). Respects .gitignore;
skips binaries and heavy dirs. Hits are `path:line tag:text`.

name: list
description: List files and directories in a path (dirs first, with sizes). Prefer this over shell `ls`. Optional recursive listing respects .gitignore and skips heavy dirs (target, node_modules, .git, …). Use `glob` for pattern search.

path.description: Directory path (relative to project root or absolute). Defaults to project root.

recursive.description: Recurse into subdirectories (default: false). Heavy dirs are pruned.

name: lsp
description: Language Server Protocol tool — diagnostics, hover, definition, references, type_definition, implementation, document/workspace symbols. Requires a language server installed for the file type.

file_path.description: Absolute path to the file to analyze

line.description: 1-indexed line number (required for hover, definition, references, type_definition, implementation)

query.description: Workspace symbol query (symbols action without file_path)

name: memory
description: Save or recall durable project facts across sessions (preferences, build commands, decisions). Prefer this over re-asking the user. Do not store secrets.

action.description: write/list/search/delete facts; learn a reusable lesson; code_search over indexed code; index the codebase for RAG

name: panel
description: Pin a file, unified diff, or mermaid diagram on the user's side panel (Preview tab). Use to keep a reference visible while you keep working. Does not edit files.

action.description: What to put on the panel

path.description: File path (show_file / show_diff). Relative to the project.

source.description: Inline mermaid source, or a unified diff when path is omitted

name: plan
description: Enter or exit planning mode (read-only, no file modifications)

action.description: Whether to enter or exit planning mode

name: question
description: Ask the user one or more clarifying questions with optional multiple-choice options. Prefer this over guessing when requirements, approach, or risk are ambiguous. Each question may set multi_select. The UI always offers an Other free-text path. Use short labels and helpful descriptions; put the recommended option first.

choices.description: Legacy string choices for the single-question form

important.description: Legacy: if true, prompt even in auto mode

multi_select.description: Legacy multi_select for the single-question form

questions.description: One or more questions (preferred). Max 4 recommended.

choices.description: Legacy: plain string options (same as options[].label)

important.description: If true, prompt even in approval_mode=auto (destructive / irreversible). Default false.

multi_select.description: Allow selecting more than one option (default false)

options.description: Choices (label + description). Other is added automatically.

preview.description: Optional extra detail shown when focused

name: read
description: Read a text file (line-numbered; a long source file returns its declaration outline first) or an internal URL: skill://, agent://, proc://, rule://, pr://, issue://, mcp:// (a bare scheme lists). Long notes: `read agent://tools/read`.

outline.description: Declaration outline instead of lines. Default: on for source files over 400 lines read without offset/limit; false forces lines, true outlines any size

path.description: File path (relative to project root or absolute), or an internal URL: skill://<name>, agent://<id>, proc://<job-id>, rule://<name>, pr://<number>[/diff], issue://<number>, mcp://<server>/<uri>

guide:
Read a text file with line numbers. Prefer project-relative paths.

Outline: a source file over 400 lines read without `offset`/`limit` returns its
declaration lines (fn/struct/class/impl/headings, indentation kept) with line
numbers and content tags, then `[file has N lines; showing its outline. ...]`.
The tags work with `edit`. Read a range next with `offset`/`limit`.
`outline: false` always pages; `outline: true` outlines a file of any length.
Extensions repomap does not map, files over 512 KB, or files with no
declarations page as usual.

Internal URLs (a bare scheme lists what it can read):
- `skill://<name>` — a skill body.
- `agent://<id>` — a finished task/swarm artifact; `agent://<id>/<json-pointer>` one
value of its structured result (e.g. `agent://task-1/findings/0/path`);
`agent://tools/<name>` this guide set.
- `proc://<job-id>` — the stored log of a background shell job
(`.whycodes/scratch/<id>.log`); `bg` lists live jobs.
- `rule://<name>` — a project rule file (`.whycodes/rules/*.md`, `.cursor/rules/*.mdc`,
`.clinerules/*.md`, `.github/instructions/*.md`).
- `pr://<number>` / `pr://<number>/diff` — a pull request of the `origin` GitHub
remote (metadata and body, or the diff); `pr://` lists the open ones (first page).
- `issue://<number>` — an issue of the same remote; `issue://` lists the open ones.
GitHub reads use the same token discovery and network allowlist as `github_pr`.
- `mcp://<server>/<uri>` — an MCP resource; `mcp://<server>` lists that server's
resources, `mcp://` the connected servers.

A `.ipynb` reads as its cells: `# %% [code] cell:N` before each source,
outputs summarized in one `# out:` line. `edit` / `write` take that text.

name: repomap
description: Signature map of a directory: declaration-like lines (fn/struct/class/impl), packed to a token budget. Use to orient before `read`. Not a full dump — bodies are omitted. Served from the live file index when warm.

max_tokens.description: Approximate token budget for the whole map (default: 4000, max: 16000)

path.description: Directory or file to map (default: project root)

name: rewind
description: End an active `checkpoint` by dropping exploratory conversation after the mark and keeping `report`. Files are not reverted.

report.description: Concise findings to keep after collapsing the investigation

name: schedule
description: After `after_secs`, either start a background shell `command` and/or queue a user `goal` prompt for the next free turn. Use for deferred checks and simple automation. Not a persistent daemon — process-local only.

after_secs.description: Delay in seconds before firing (default 0, max 86400)

command.description: Shell command to run in the background when the timer fires

description.description: Short label for the scheduled job

goal.description: User prompt to enqueue for the next free agent turn

name: shell
description: Run a shell command. Long notes: `read agent://tools/bash`.

background.description: If true, start the command in the background and return a job id immediately

description.description: Short description of why this command is run (optional)

timeout.description: Timeout in seconds (default: 120; ignored when background=true)

guide:
Execute a shell command in the project environment.

Default: wait for stdout/stderr (timeout 120s).
`background=true` returns a job id immediately; use `bg` to list/read/kill.
Long-running non-catastrophic commands auto-detach after 20s unless
`[tools.bash] auto_background = false`. Catastrophic commands (rm -rf /,
git clean of home, …) stay in the foreground and still hit the permission gate.
Child processes do not inherit provider API keys. Detached output lives under
`.whycodes/scratch`, not the OS temp dir.

name: skill
description: List or load project/user skills. Prefer `read skill://<name>` for the body; `action=list` shows names and descriptions only.

action.description: Action: 'list' shows all available skills, 'load' loads a specific skill by name

name.description: Name of the skill to load (required when action is 'load')

name: swarm
description: Run several subagents in parallel on independent units of work. In a git repo each worker gets an isolated worktree under `.whycodes/swarm/`; changes three-way-merge back into the main checkout (conflicts toast). Without git (or with worktrees off), workers share the checkout and file claims block double-writes. Prefer for wide audits or mechanical migrations across disjoint paths. For a single investigation use `task` instead.

max_concurrent.description: Max workers running at once (default from config, usually 4)

context.description: Optional extra context for this worker

max_turns.description: Max conversation turns for this worker (default: 15)

paths.description: Optional paths to pre-claim before the worker starts (reduces mid-turn conflicts)

subagent_type.description: general (default), explore, scout, or a name from the system prompt's `# Custom agents` list

name: swarm_msg
description: Send a short message to another swarm worker (`to` = worker-N), the parent agent (`parent`), or every sibling (`all`). Use when your work affects someone else. Not a chat — one or two sentences.

name: task
description: Launch a subagent to handle a complex multi-step task. Use for research, exploration, or parallel units of work. Prefer explore for read-only codebase search, general for multi-step work that may edit files.

goal.description: The goal or task for the subagent to accomplish

max_turns.description: Maximum conversation turns for the subagent (default: 15)

output_schema.description: JSON Schema (object) for a typed result. The subagent ends with a matching ```json block (plus a required `what_i_did_not_check` string array); it is validated, retried once if invalid, returned after the summary and readable as `read agent://<id>/<json-pointer>`. Overrides a custom agent's `output`.

subagent_type.description: general (default), explore, scout, or a name from the system prompt's `# Custom agents` list

name: todo
description: Create and manage a structured task list. The user sees this list live at the top of the session. Use for any task with 3+ steps. Mark the current item in_progress (only one) and completed as soon as the step is done. Default merge=true updates items by id.

merge.description: If true (default), merge with existing todos by id; if false, replace entirely

id.description: Unique identifier for the todo item

name: todoread
description: Read the current todo list for this session

name: todowrite
description: Create and manage a structured task list. The user sees this list live at the top of the session. Use for any task with 3+ steps. Mark the current item in_progress (only one) and completed as soon as the step is done. Default merge=true updates items by id.

merge.description: If true (default), merge with existing todos by id; if false, replace entirely

id.description: Unique identifier for the todo item

name: tool_search
description: Discover tools not in the core profile (apply_patch, memory, schedule, swarm, web, browser, github, lsp, git_*, plan, …) and activate them for this session. Actions: search (keywords), select (name or comma-separated names), list (activated + deferred catalogue).

query.description: Keywords for search, or tool name(s) for select (comma-separated)

name: truncate
description: Truncate long output to fit context window

max_chars.description: Maximum number of characters to keep (default: 8000)

max_lines.description: Maximum number of lines to keep (default: 200)

name: webfetch
description: Fetch content from a URL and return readable text. Prefers machine-readable responses (JSON, Markdown, plain text) via Accept headers. For package versions prefer registry APIs (e.g. https://registry.npmjs.org/<pkg>/latest) or GitHub Releases over marketing HTML pages. If a site exposes llm.txt / llms.txt, fetch that URL when you need LLM-oriented docs.

name: websearch
description: Search the web and return result snippets. The engine comes from `[websearch]` config; by default SerpAPI when SERPAPI_API_KEY is set, else DuckDuckGo HTML. For 'latest version' questions: do not pin the query to a past calendar year (e.g. avoid '2024'/'2025'); search 'Nuxt latest release' or fetch canonical APIs via webfetch (npm registry, GitHub Releases, official docs).

query.description: The search query. Prefer current phrasing without a past year for 'latest' lookups.

name: worktree
description: Git worktree helpers under `.whycodes/worktrees/`. Actions: create, list, remove, enter (switch tool cwd), exit (restore project root). Use to isolate experimental edits without touching the main checkout.

name: write
description: Write content to a file, creating it if it doesn't exist.

content.description: Content to write to the file

path.description: Path to the file to write
